summary: Paul Demiéville worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at King's College London and under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. His posts included director at Hōbōgirin (around 1929–1979) and chair at the Collège de France (1946–1964).

Paul Deussen was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Bonn under Christian Lassen (around 1864–1866) and at Humboldt University of Berlin (around 1867–1869). He was a professor at the University of Kiel from around 1889 to 1919.
Paul Dundas was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He served as a professor at the University of Edinburgh from around 1976 to 2017.

Paul Fredericq was a historian who studied at Koninklijk Atheneum Voskenslaan, Ghent University, and the University of Liège around 1871–1875. He held posts at the University of Liège (around 1879–1883) and Ghent University (around 1883–1919).
Paul Fuller is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Bristol, studying under doctoral supervisor Rupert Gethin and teacher Paul Dundas.

Paul G. Hackett works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies and studied at Columbia University. He held positions at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and Columbia University (attested 2003, 2016).

Paul Groner is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo in 1973 and earned a PhD from Yale University. He served as a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1982–1996 and 2009–2010).

Paul Hacker was an Indologist and philosopher who studied in Bonn, Heidelberg, Frankfurt, and Berlin. He held posts at Münster (1950, 1963–1978), the Mithila Research Institute (1954), Bonn (chair, 1955), and Pennsylvania (visiting professor, 1971).

Paul Harrison specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. He studied at the University of Auckland and the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. He later held posts at Auckland, Canterbury, and Stanford University.

Paul J. Griffiths works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Oxford and Wisconsin–Madison under Minoru Kiyota. His posts included the University of Chicago, Notre Dame, University of Illinois Chicago, and Duke University.
Paul Kingsbury is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2002), where he studied under doctoral supervisor George Cardona.

Paul L. Swanson is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD from Wisconsin–Madison under Minoru Kiyota and also studied at Otani University. He held long-term posts at Nanzan University and the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture (around 1986–2021).

Paul Mendes-Flohr worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University. He held academic positions at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (around 1973–2006) and the University of Chicago (around 1999–2024).

Paul Mus was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied under Jean Przyluski, Sylvain Lévi, and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at the EPHE (1937), Collège de France (1946), and Yale University (around 1950–1969).
Paul Nietupski is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his PhD from Columbia University and held a post at John Carroll University (attested 2008).

Paul Pelliot was a sinologist and Central Asian studies scholar who studied in Paris, including under Émile Senart and Édouard Chavannes. His posts included the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1901) and the Collège de France (1909, 1911–1945).

Paul Regnaud was an Indologist and linguist who studied as an élève at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 1870–1876. He subsequently held a post at the University of Lyon from around 1879 to 1908.
Paul Rouzer is a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts at Harvard University and the University of Minnesota (attested 2007).

Paul Thieme was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen. He held academic posts at Breslau, Halle-Wittenberg, Goethe University Frankfurt, and the University of Tübingen (1960–1973).

Paul Tillich was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Berlin, Tübingen, Breslau, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at the University of Berlin, Frankfurt (1929–1933), Union Theological Seminary (1933–1955), Harvard (around 1955–1962), and Chicago (around 1962–1965).
